resolvedClarifications.question: What is the exact text of the error message displayed when the user submits the form with an empty Username field?
What is the exact text of the error message displayed when the user submits the form with an empty Password field?
The requirement uses the word 'recommended' for the
Should the Login button be enabled at all times regardless of form state, or should it only become active/enabled once both the Username and Password fields are populated?
Is the login page required to be functional and tested on mobile viewports (e.g. 375px), or is the scope limited to desktop devices only?
What is the exact visible text of the 'contact support' instruction shown to the locked-out user — is it part of the error message string itself, or a separate element on the page?
resolvedClarifications.answer: Epic sadface: Sorry, this user has been locked out.

resolvedClarifications.question: What is the measurable latency threshold (in milliseconds or seconds) that defines the expected slow-load behaviour for performance_glitch_user — i.e. what value distinguishes a pass from a fail?
Under what conditions is the error icon displayed (always with every error, or only for specific error types)? What is the visible or accessible label/alt text of the error icon?
Is #E2453C the required (mandatory) colour for error message text, or is it merely a suggestion that allows other red shades?

If the Username field contains only whitespace characters (e.g. spaces) and is submitted after trimming, which error message is displayed — 'Epic sadface: Username is required' or a different message?
What is the URL path of the login page (e.g. '/', '/login', '/index.html') that tests should navigate to as a precondition?

Given that scope is confirmed as desktop only, should the '320px to 2560px viewport width' range in Section 3.2 and the '375px mobile' reference in Section 2.5.1 be treated as out of scope entirely, or is there a minimum desktop viewport width that must be tested?
What is the exact visible text content of the Credentials Info Box on the login page (e.g. the full string listing usernames and the password hint)?
resolvedClarifications.answer:
Accepted usernames are:
standard_user
locked_out_user
problem_user
performance_glitch_user
error_user
visual_user
Password for all users:
secret_sauce

resolvedClarifications.question: Is there a separate visible UI element (e.g. a link, a second line of text) instructing the locked-out user to contact support, distinct from the error message string 'Epic sadface: Sorry, this user has been locked out.'? If so, what is its exact visible text?
resolvedClarifications.answer: No. This is the exact error message - "Epic sadface: Sorry, this user has been locked out" which get displayed when user tries to login in

resolvedClarifications.question: Confirmed via resolved clarification that #E2453C is mandatory — no further action needed. Raised only to document the textual contradiction between 'recommended' in the spec and the resolved answer.

Resolved clarification states to ignore the latency threshold. This scenario can only be verified as a functional login (redirect to /inventory.html occurs) without a performance assertion. Is that the intended test scope for performance_glitch_user?
Are error messages displayed as an in-page styled element (part of the DOM) or as a browser-native alert() dialog? And are they positioned below the form fields or below the Login button?
resolvedClarifications.answer: part of the DOM. Position is over the password text box.

resolvedClarifications.question: Confirmed via resolved clarification: the Login button is always enabled. This ambiguity is recorded for traceability only — no further action required.
resolvedClarifications.answer: On the Login page, the login button will always remain enabled.

resolvedClarifications.question: What is the expected mechanism for screen-reader announcement of error messages — e.g. an aria-live region (assertive or polite), role='alert', or another ARIA attribute — and is there a specific attribute value the test should assert?

Confirmed via resolved clarification: the contact-support instruction is conveyed entirely by the error message 'Epic sadface: Sorry, this user has been locked out.' with no separate element. No further action required.
resolvedClarifications.answer: Yes. There is not separate element.

resolvedClarifications.question: Is the Swag Labs Logo a static image only, or does it have an interactive function (e.g. clicking it navigates somewhere)? If interactive, what is the expected behaviour?

What are the specific visual inconsistencies expected on the product catalog page after problem_user logs in, and how should they be verified (e.g. specific broken images, wrong text, specific element states)?
resolvedClarifications.answer: Same image is displayed on the inventory page for all product.

resolvedClarifications.question: What are the specific visual glitches expected on the inventory page after visual_user logs in, and how should they be verified?
resolvedClarifications.answer: Test keyword is used as prefix in one of the product name.

resolvedClarifications.question: Should each test precondition ensure the user is fully logged out before navigating to https://www.saucedemo.com/? If so, what is the visible indicator that confirms no active session exists (e.g. the login form is displayed, a specific page title, or a URL check)?
What is the expected login behaviour for 'error_user' — does it succeed (redirect to /inventory.html), fail with a specific error message, or produce some other observable outcome?
resolvedClarifications.answer: Yes login will succeed. But user will not be able to add some product to cart.

resolvedClarifications.question: What is the exact URL path (relative or absolute) that the user lands on after a successful login — e.g. https://admin.nexolvi.ai/dashboard?
resolvedClarifications.answer: The URL is https://admin.nexolvi.ai/, but the page has header - Dashboard

resolvedClarifications.question: What is the observable user-facing behaviour that confirms the Remember Me session is active — for example, does the user land directly on the Dashboard on a subsequent visit without seeing the login form, or is there another visible indicator?
resolvedClarifications.answer: the user land directly on the Dashboard on a subsequent visit without seeing the login form

resolvedClarifications.question: Where exactly on the login page is the 'Login failed' error message displayed — e.g. above the form, between the fields and the button, or below the Sign In button? Is it an inline element, a toast notification, or a banner?
resolvedClarifications.answer: above the form in a alert box

resolvedClarifications.question: Does the Sign In button become enabled as soon as any non-empty string is typed in the Email field (regardless of email format), or does the field require a syntactically valid email address (containing '@' and a domain) before the button is enabled?
resolvedClarifications.answer: as soon as any non-empty string is typed in the Email field and the Password field

resolvedClarifications.question: When the Remember Me checkbox is NOT selected, what is the expected session behaviour — e.g. session expires when the browser is closed, or after a specific idle timeout period?
resolvedClarifications.answer: session expires when the browser is closed and on new session user lands on the Login page
